result: The official SEP-2663 task lifecycle defines capability negotiation as the client declaring io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks and the server advertising the same extension, followed by task creation and client polling via tasks/get. In the reviewed specification text, clients SHOULD respect pollIntervalMs, but no client MUST/SHOULD perform a separate ServerCapabilities::supports_tasks-style preflight immediately before tasks/get once a task handle has been returned. At modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk@4a738b9dd99eaca418b614afa433a0cbdaf8d056, server-side validate_tasks_capability gates tasks/* on the server's advertised tasks capability and the client's declared tasks capability, while worker194 established that Peer<RoleClient>::get_task sends GetTaskRequest directly without such a caller-side preflight. In this exact scope, a caller-side server-capability check is defensive rather than a normative prerequisite for polling a returned task handle.
source_scope: Own clean state, frozen sanitized root/control identities, own role config, official public task protocol documentation, and exact-commit public repository source only.
scope_guard: Exact tested scope is the reviewed SEP-2663 capability-negotiation/polling text as retrieved on 2026-09-07 plus the pinned rust-sdk task gate/client flow. No claim about all MCP versions, all callers/SDKs, deployed connectors, scheduler parity, server conformance, persistence, idempotency, external effects, or default-branch behavior.
